players_projections_seasonal <- players_projections_seasonal_average_merged %>%

## Univariate Cluster Analysis: RB Player Tiers (Based on Projected Points)

Perform a univariate cluster analysis to identify tiers of RBs based on projected points.
Determine how many tiers provide an optimal tradeoff of fit and parsimony for the following criteria: BIC, ICL, and bootstrap.

```{r}
tiersRB_bic <- mclust::mclustBIC(
  data = players_projections_seasonal_rb$points,
  G = 1:9
)

tiersRB_bic
summary(tiersRB_bic)
plot(tiersRB_bic)

tiersRB_icl <- mclust::mclustICL(
  data = players_projections_seasonal_rb$points,
  G = 1:9
)

tiersRB_icl
summary(tiersRB_icl)
plot(tiersRB_icl)

tiersRB_bootstrap <- mclust::mclustBootstrapLRT(
  data = players_projections_seasonal_rb$points,
  modelName = "V") # variable/unequal variance (for univariate data)

tiersRB_bootstrap

plot(
  tiersRB_bootstrap,
  G = 3)

plot(
  tiersRB_bootstrap,
  G = 4)
```

How many tiers are recommend based on BIC?
How many tiers are recommend based on ICL?
How many tiers are recommend based on bootstrapping?

Now, set the number of tiers to the optimal number of tiers identified by bootstrapping.

```{r}
numTiersRB <- as.numeric(summary(tiersRB_bootstrap)[,"Length"][1]) # or could specify the number of teams manually
```

Now, fit a cluster model to this number of RB tiers.

```{r}
clusterModelRBs <- mclust::Mclust(
  data = players_projections_seasonal_rb$points,
  G = numTiersRB,
)

table(clusterModelRBs$classification)
```

How many players are in each tier?

Create a plot of these tiers.

```{r}
players_projections_seasonal_rb$tier <- clusterModelRBs$classification

players_projections_seasonal_rb <- players_projections_seasonal_rb %>%
  mutate(
    tier = factor(max(tier, na.rm = TRUE) + 1 - tier),
    fullname = paste(first_name, last_name, sep = " ")
  )

players_projections_seasonal_rb$position_rank <- rank(
  players_projections_seasonal_rb$points * -1,
  na.last = "keep",
  ties.method = "min")

plot_rbTiers <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  data = players_projections_seasonal_rb,
  mapping = aes(
    x = points,
    y = position_rank,
    color = tier
  )) +
  geom_point(
    aes(
      text = fullname # add player name for mouse over tooltip
  )) +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = "reverse") +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    x = "Projected Points",
    y = "Position Rank",
    title = "Running Back Fantasy Points by Tier",
    color = "Tier") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

plotly::ggplotly(plot_rbTiers)
```

Tiers are intended to be helpful for aiding you in your draft to identify groups of players that are indistinguishable.
It isn't very helpful, in a draft, if you have too many or too few players in a given tier.
Looking at the plot, would you say there are too many tiers or too few tiers to be useful?
That is, are there too many players or too few players in each tier?

Modify your cluster model to be more useful by changing (i.e., manually specifying) the number of tiers.

```{r}
clusterModelRBs_new <- mclust::Mclust(
  data = players_projections_seasonal_rb$points,
  G = INSERT,
)

table(clusterModelRBs_new$classification)
```

How many players are in each tier?

Create a plot of these tiers.

```{r}
players_projections_seasonal_rb$tier2 <- clusterModelRBs_new$classification

players_projections_seasonal_rb <- players_projections_seasonal_rb %>%
  mutate(
    tier2 = factor(max(tier2, na.rm = TRUE) + 1 - tier2),
    fullname = paste(first_name, last_name, sep = " ")
  )

plot_rbTiers2 <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  data = players_projections_seasonal_rb,
  mapping = aes(
    x = points,
    y = position_rank,
    color = tier2
  )) +
  geom_point(
    aes(
      text = fullname # add player name for mouse over tooltip
  )) +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = "reverse") +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    x = "Projected Points",
    y = "Position Rank",
    title = "Running Back Fantasy Points by Tier",
    color = "Tier") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

plotly::ggplotly(plot_rbTiers2)
```

## Multivariate Cluster Analysis: Types of WRs

First, let's prepare the data for cluster analysis.
We select the variables, average across seasons for a player, join with the player's name, and exclude missing values (which are not permissable by cluster analysis).

```{r}
player_stats_seasonal_wr_cluster <- player_stats_seasonal %>%
  filter(position_group == "WR") %>% 
  select(player_id, receptions, targets, receiving_yards, receiving_tds, receiving_air_yards, receiving_yards_after_catch, receiving_first_downs, receiving_epa, racr, target_share, air_yards_share, wopr) %>% 
  group_by(player_id) %>% 
  summarise(across(everything(), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)))

player_stats_seasonal_wr_cluster <- left_join(
  player_stats_seasonal_wr_cluster,
  nfl_playerIDs[,c("gsis_id","name")],
  by = c("player_id" = "gsis_id")
) %>% 
  na.omit()
```

Next, perform a multivariate cluster analysis to determine how many clusters/types of WRs provide an optimal tradeoff between fit and parsimony.

```{r}
wrTypes_bic <- mclust::mclustBIC(
  data = player_stats_seasonal_wr_cluster %>% select(-player_id, -name),
  G = 1:9
)

wrTypes_bic
summary(wrTypes_bic)
plot(wrTypes_bic)

wrTypes_icl <- mclust::mclustICL(
  data = player_stats_seasonal_wr_cluster %>% select(-player_id, -name),
  G = 1:9
)

wrTypes_icl
summary(wrTypes_icl)
plot(wrTypes_icl)

#wrTypes_bootstrap <- mclust::mclustBootstrapLRT( # this takes a while to run
#  data = player_stats_seasonal_wr_cluster %>% select(-player_id, -name),
#  modelName = "VEV") # ellipsoidal with equal volume, variable shape, and equal orientation (for multivariate data)
#
#wrTypes_bootstrap
#
#plot(
#  wrTypes_bootstrap,
#  G = 3)
#
#plot(
#  wrTypes_bootstrap,
#  G = 4)
```

How many clusters of WRs would be selected based on BIC?
How many clusters of WRs would be selected based on ICL?
How many clusters of WRs would be selected based on bootstrapped likelihood ratio tests?

Now, perform the multivariate cluster analysis with three clusters.

```{r}
clusterModelWRtypes <- mclust::Mclust(
  data = player_stats_seasonal_wr_cluster %>% select(-player_id, -name),
  G = 3,
)

summary(clusterModelWRtypes)

plot(
  clusterModelWRtypes,
  what = "BIC")

plot(
  clusterModelWRtypes,
  what = "classification")

plot(
  clusterModelWRtypes,
  what = "uncertainty")

plot(
  clusterModelWRtypes,
  what = "density")

table(clusterModelWRtypes$classification)
```

How many players are in each cluster?

Provide the average stats for each cluster.

```{r}
player_stats_seasonal_wr_cluster$type <- clusterModelWRtypes$classification

player_stats_seasonal_wr_cluster %>% 
  group_by(type) %>% 
  summarise(across(
    where(is.numeric),
    ~ mean(., na.rm = TRUE)
    )) %>% 
  t() %>% 
  round(., 2)
```

How would you characterize each cluster?

Provide the names of the players in each cluster.

```{r}
player_stats_seasonal_wr_cluster %>% 
  filter(type == 1) %>% 
  select(name)

player_stats_seasonal_wr_cluster %>% 
  filter(type == 2) %>% 
  select(name)
```
